clauses.reason: The operative paragraph reads "I hereby exempt the said William H. Egberts from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1939." The exemption is a one-time permission for a fixed period and the period is stated in the order itself. By its own terms it runs through September 30, 1939, recorded inclusive under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; the exclusive reading ends it when September 30, 1939 begins. State on 2026-10-14: terminated, the permission having been exhausted by lapse of the stated period.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 7950 of August 9, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts William H. Egberts from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1939, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 362912, Common Crawl capture 2025-05-19T22:34:59Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7950, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on September 30, 1939; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The OFR catalog search and the held-text name search both report zero hits for this order, so no revoking, superseding or extending instrument is recorded in the packet.
